newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean rally cools off, shares end lower.
newsitem.headline: Chilean rally cools off, shares end lower.

text.p: Chilean shares seesawed through the day and closed narrowly lower as a record-breaking rally began to peter out, brokers said.
Electrical shares, stars of the bull run sweeping the bolsa since mid-May, were mostly lower as the blue-chip IPSA index ended 0.11 percent lower at 133.27 in the second straight daily decline.

"The rises in electrical shares are starting to run out of steam in the short-term and we could even see a slight correction," said Enrique Danioni, analyst at brokers Sud Americano. "I don't think we'll see any steep falls but the rises will be a bit more regular."
The all-share IGPA index ended 0.06 percent lower at 5722.57 points on strong volume of 23 billion pesos.

Danioni said medium-term prospects for the bolsa were still for growth, especially with expectations for a small cut in interest rates this month or next and inflation and economic growth at near-optimum levels.
"The signal on inflation yesterday was quite encouraging. It's a good moment for a reduction in interest rates," Danioni said, referring to inflation figures showing a 0.2 percent rise in May.
Among electrical shares, Endesa eased 0.3 percent to 313 pesos and Chilgener slipped 1.4 percent to 172 pesos. Enersis rose 1.3 percent over Tuesday's close to 299 pesos.

Paper companies were down, with pulp and oil conglomerate Copec down 1.6 percent to 1,845 pesos and CMPC off one percent to 4750 pesos on renewed expectations of a decline in pulp prices, brokers said.
Banco Santiago was up 3.5 percent from Tuesday's close to 10.50 pesos after newspaper reports said the Central Bank would not sell its shares in the private bank until sometime in the third quarter.
